status: Test-only planning traces. Placeholder field names, not contract 0.1.0 and not the future P0-08 contract. Synthetic; no model output, no user data.

step_forms.event: apply a context event (see disclosure-model.ts Event)
step_forms.generate: snapshot an item at generation time from the current context (problem, version, attempt, revision, preference key, active request); optional show / queueVoice / cache
step_forms.present: check decide() for a previously generated item at this moment
step_forms.cache: cacheHit() for the active request; expect the id of the cached item it may reuse, or null
step_forms.surfaces: revalidate shown items and the voice queue after the preceding events; expect withdrawn/flushed ids
step_forms.expectPreferenceKey: the effective language/preference key of the current context

traces.note: The server accepted the offline request and it is still current, so the reconnect snapshot carries it. (Since the P0-12 QA follow-up, accepted means applied; the snapshot's request says what is current. See accepted-then-closed-by-another-device.)

covers: A43 (disclosure side only; entry linkage is not modeled)

traces.note: Lead-reported sequence (integration review of 4c32e49), extended with further snapshots.
Positive control: the user's own later explicit request is answered at its level; a stale snapshot does not replace it.
An offline close then an offline lower-level request that the server did not accept: the old full-solution snapshot must not come back.
Accepting the later offline request (still current in the snapshot) also acknowledges the earlier offline close; a newer server request then applies normally.
Returning to an attempt does not accept an older snapshot for it.
Liveness: once the server acknowledges the close (here in a resync while already connected), a causally later server request applies again.

AUDIO-14: a request heard in a late/backfilled transcript keeps its historical time and cannot open or escalate help, restore closed permission or resolve an unsynced close. The user's own later live request still works.
QA P012-D1 S1. A connected 'let me try' is pending until acknowledged; a reconnect at the version the device had before saying it cannot contain it.

QA P012-D1 S1b and S4. Newer snapshots without causal proof of the close (still carrying the old request, or a late unordered request from another device) cannot reopen help; only an acknowledgement or a causally later accepted request can.

QA P012-D1 S1c. The user's own lower request is pending: a same-version reconnect or a newer snapshot without proof cannot bring back the older full solution. Once the server echoes the request, a later server request applies again.
QA P012-D2. The reconnect snapshot says the offline request was accepted (applied) but its current state is closed, e.g. 'let me try' on the iPhone ordered after it. Accepted is not current.

QA P012-D5 (a), liveness. An unsynced close, then the user's later connected request; the server echoing that request as current proves it has both intents, so a causally later iPhone request is shown.
QA H2. An older snapshot that arrives late is superseded together with its acknowledgement, and an acknowledgement for another attempt does not apply here.

QA P012-D5 (b). An offline close; the server acknowledges it while the user is on p2. After returning, help does not carry over, but a later server request for p1 applies without the acknowledgement being repeated.

An offline lower request that the server did not accept is no longer answered, but it still limits what the server may show until a later intent is acknowledged: the older full solution stays blocked, a lower server request may show.
ADR 0002 unknown order stays restrictive: a newer snapshot that does not contain the user's request may lower or close it, never widen it; the echo restores the server's authority.
Liveness. A reconnect at the version the device had when the user asked is known to be older than the request, so it neither answers nor restricts it.
A cached voice segment is never reused to answer a request; a cached card at the same binding is.
While the user is on p2, a newer p1 snapshot without the acknowledgement arrives first; an older p1 snapshot with it arrives late and is superseded, so the close still stands after returning.
